title: Witnesses who have gone to Congress, and what the record corroborates
notes: Stewart's 18 September scope ruling. jason-sands has no edge and must stop being an island. Each witness's route to Congress is recorded, and michael-herrera's edge to the 2025 hearing is not a witness appearance.

lead.text: Since David Grusch's sworn testimony in July 2023, witnesses have taken UAP accounts to Congress by different routes: some sworn at open hearings, like Dylan Borland, Jeffrey Nuccetelli and George Knapp on 9 September 2025, and some only on paper, like Michael Herrera, whose written testimony, supplied by Steven Greer, a member entered into the record without his appearing.

summary.text: The 9 September 2025 hearing of the House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets is the centre of the topic: its sworn witnesses described encounters and reprisals, one named a contractor and two people as gatekeepers, and a member entered further testimonies supplied by Steven Greer.

What the record corroborates differs witness by witness: a hearing record fixes that a person testified and when; for what they described, the board mostly has their own word, with the documents they cite unreleased.

The routes to Congress are part of the story: Grusch went through inspectors general before testifying, AARO counts as its top tier those interviewees who spoke to Congress first and were referred on, and several witnesses moved between independent media and a private foundation's platform.

Some names in this topic are claimed witnesses whose appearance before Congress no record establishes, such as Jason Sands, and Jake Barber, who says he gave testimony in a closed setting to a committee he does not name.

record.text: The printed record of the 9 September 2025 hearing, Serial No. 119-44, lists as witnesses Jeffrey Nuccetelli, U.S. Air Force veteran; Chief Alexandro Wiggins, U.S. Navy; George Knapp, UAP journalist; Dylan Borland, UAP witness and Air Force veteran; and Joe Spielberger of the Project on Government Oversight as the minority witness.
Borland, Nuccetelli and Knapp appear as sworn witnesses, and Borland and Nuccetelli filed written testimony with the Task Force.

Herrera is not a witness at that hearing. The record shows Rep. Eric Burlison entering testimonies he said Greer had given him, Herrera's among them, admitted without objection; Herrera is on no committee witness list, and his name appears once across the three hearing records.

Burlison asked Borland on the record whether BAASS Systems was involved in reverse engineering exploitation of non-human intelligence craft; Borland testified that before Grusch and the disclosure process, suppression of witnesses was probably extremely widespread.

The same record's index lists a letter to the Secretary of Defense regarding reprisal against Grusch, submitted by Rep. Crane. Grusch attended but did not testify, and Knapp said from the witness table that extra-legal acts against witnesses are carried out by persons unknown, as Grusch knew, including events in recent days; no member asked what he meant.

H.R. 5060, the UAP Whistleblower Protection Act, was introduced on 29 August 2025 by Rep. Tim Burchett with Reps. Luna and Crane, and referred to Oversight, Armed Services and Intelligence; Burlison said on the record that such language is blocked again and again, often by staff rather than elected officials.

The July 2023 hearing record lists Grusch as a former NRO representative to the UAP Task Force; his public statements had been cleared for open publication by DoD prepublication review in April 2023; and Burlison named him Special Advisor to his office on 27 March 2025.

AARO's historical report says it had interviewed about 30 people by 17 September 2023, and that its Tier 1 interviewees are those who spoke with congressional staff or Members and were then referred to AARO.

The Sol Foundation's 2025 symposium, held 24 to 27 October 2025, listed Karl Nell, Jake Barber, Dylan Borland and Jeff Nuccetelli among its speakers, and the foundation published Nell's paper calling for government disclosure in May 2025.

claimed.text: Borland testified that in 2012, at the base where he worked, he saw a 100-foot equilateral triangle of what he called fluid material take off, and that after reporting it his career was deliberately obstructed and he endured more than a decade of reprisals. He says he complained to AARO in March 2023 and to the Intelligence Community Inspector General in August 2023.

After the hearing, Borland told Jesse Michels that AARO had sent ODNI an uncorrected record of his interview although it had accepted his corrections, and argued that his account coming back unclassified is itself evidence about what he saw; the board records the second point as his argument only. Michels ran a three-episode sequence with him in August 2026.

Nuccetelli testified that between 2003 and 2005, during NRO launches at Vandenberg, objects like flying buildings pulsed and moved strangely; that on 14 October 2003 Boeing contractors reported a glowing red square hovering over two missile defence sites; that each incident was documented and reported up the chain; that one witness was threatened into silence; and that Air Force records of it are held by AARO and the FBI.

Knapp testified that documents tell a different story from what the public and Congress have been told and that the material had been moved to private contractors. Asked which corporations hold it, he named Lockheed and offered a list; asked for gatekeepers, he named Dr. James Ryder at Lockheed and Glenn Gaffney of the CIA. He also said he had confirmed that Robert Bigelow negotiated with Lockheed executives to receive unusual material held in California.

Grusch testified under oath in 2023 that he was informed in the course of his duties of a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse engineering programme and denied read-on, that he based his claims on interviewing over 40 witnesses over four years, and that he had people with first-hand knowledge make their own protected disclosures to the Inspector General.

How Barber reached the record: Michels published his helicopter-retrieval account in January 2025, and he then spoke at the Sol Foundation symposium. He says his account was given to AARO and shared with Congress in a closed setting without naming the committee, that he worked under a cover contract through the Bureau of Indian Affairs, and that he and colleagues submitted a ghost-written historical novel to prepublication review in pieces to probe who controls which information.

Karl Nell, the Army's liaison to the UAP Task Force, said on the record in June 2023 that Grusch is beyond reproach and that his account of an eighty-year reverse-engineering arms race is fundamentally correct, and has said that non-human intelligence exists and has been interacting with humanity.

Jason Sands describes himself on a podcast as a retired Air Force master sergeant with 22 years' service; the sceptic Brian Dunning gives the same rank and length of service independently, which the board treats as weak convergence on the service claim only.

Herrera's own account is on a dated podcast recording of July 2023; the board infers, without any record making the link, that he is the anonymous interviewee AARO summarises on page 29 of its historical report.

Burlison has offered his office's help to current and former employees and contractors who want to come forward, and recommends that they ask for a member of Congress to be present as well as an attorney; he names Gaffney as the first person he would want to question in a closed setting. Eric Davis, who says he had no direct interaction with Gaffney, has described him as very antagonistic to an aerospace firm's proposed release of crash-retrieval materials.

The committee's published hearing wrap-up, summarising the testimony, asserts that agencies withheld information, that witnesses face retaliation, that UAP spending flows to private entities outside the reach of FOIA, and that personnel lack standardised reporting protocols.

contested.text: The Herrera edge is not a witness appearance, and promotional claims that he is testifying to Congress are unsupported; he has never been a hearing witness.

Sands's two most repeated credentials, an appearance in the documentary The Program and testimony to Congress, the ICIG or AARO, are established by no opened record, and no witness list names him. Dunning itemises claims by Sands that he rejects, including that the Wilson-Davis memo is genuine, and says Sands first claimed and then contradicted involvement with the Navy's UAP Task Force.

Knapp's naming is sworn and specific but its sourcing has not been published; no corporate record confirms Ryder's role at Lockheed, and neither Ryder nor Lockheed has responded. AARO's report says executives and chief technology officers of the named companies denied the allegations to its Director.

AARO records an unnamed interviewee's claim that a former senior CIA official quashed the proposal to move the material from the corporation; AARO does not name the official, and whether that official is Gaffney is not established.

The official response to Grusch runs the other way: the Department said in June 2023 that AARO had not discovered any verifiable information substantiating a possession or reverse-engineering programme; AARO records at least eight approaches to Grusch and concluded he had no intention of providing information; and Rep. Grothman later said that no agency had been able to substantiate Grusch's claims.

On the board's reading, the path from independent media to a private foundation's platform is short and documented: Barber went from a YouTube channel in January 2025 to the Sol symposium nine months later, and Borland from the symposium to a three-episode podcast run.

questions: Does AARO hold the Vandenberg security forces records Nuccetelli says it holds, and was his account ever logged in its case holdings?
Which committee, if any, heard Jake Barber in a closed setting, and when?
What is Dr. James Ryder's role at Lockheed Martin, and what list did Knapp offer to give Congress?
What were the events in recent days against Grusch that Knapp referred to from the witness table?
Did Borland's complaints to AARO and the ICIG produce any finding, and what are his unit and dates of service?
Has Jason Sands given testimony to Congress, the ICIG or AARO, and does he appear in the documentary he is said to appear in?
Were Herrera or any of the others whose testimonies were entered by Burlison ever interviewed in a closed congressional setting?
Have any of the roughly 40 witnesses Grusch says he interviewed been heard by any committee?
George Knapp worked as a consultant to BAASS, the contractor at the centre of the Lockheed transfer he describes: how far does his reporting of that episode rest on what he learned in that role?
